That wholesale revision replaced the subsection Section 4(c) of EO 11434 had amended, a held later event on part of this clause that the packet dossier's chain lists (EO:11636, Section 21) and the claim neither records nor analyses. packet-v2 dossier EO:11434 (clauses, chain events, FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT on EO 12363)
reasoning: Identity (No. 11434, November 8, 1968, 33 FR 16485, Foreign Service personnel systems) matches the held FR text. The inventory override is correct: the dossier omitted Section 1 and split Section 4; the five restated clauses cover all operative text. Sections 1, 3 and 5 end by EO 12292 Sec. 10(i), recorded at its stated effective date 1981-02-15 with the signing date disclosed; Sections 2 and 4 survive until EO 12363 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11264 as amended on 1982-05-21, matching the OFR note 'Revoked in part by: ... EO 12363, May 21, 1982', which resolves the dossier's whole-versus-partial conflict; EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is correctly a later formal disposition; EO 12107 is a correctly dated later amendment; no savings clause appears. The outcome dates look supportable. The claim is rejected because Section 4's analysis omits a held later event: EO 11636 (effective on publication, December 24, 1971) rewrote subsection (d) of Section 21 of EO 11264 in full, displacing the substitution Section 4(c) had made. The dossier chain listed EO 11636 against Section 21, and neither the clause's later_events nor the earlier_end_check addresses it. A secondary defect is a quotation of EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) that drops a space present in the held bytes. Notes (not verdict): whether the Foreign Service Act of 1980 extinguished Section 2's reference to 'Foreign Service information officers' before 1982 is not shown by held bytes; the claim's treatment is reasonable. The quotation of EO 12363 Sec. 3 normalises OCR spacing ('O rder') and matches the held APP text exactly.

reasoning: Identity (No. 13322, December 30, 2003, 69 FR 231, Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay) and the 16-segment inventory are correct; the schedules are image-only in the held text and are incorporated by Sec. 1-6. EO 13332 Sec. 8 expressly supersedes the whole order, the OFR note 'Superseded by: EO 13332, March 3, 2004' is addressed, no earlier instrument is held, and the disclosed alternative reading (replacement of rates as of the January 2004 schedule dates) and the savings analysis are reasonable. But every first_end.date and the whole_order_end.date read 2001-03-03, which is not the date of the cited ending instrument, precedes the order's own signing, and contradicts the claim's own judgment_reason and research_rationale (2004-03-03). The dated fields are wrong, so the claim is rejected. With 2004-03-03 in those fields, the claim would appear supportable.
